SddModule.keywords: module, authoring, decomposition, entity, dbc, sdd-new, sdd-check
SddModule.Mission: Materialize the smallest cohesive module hierarchy from an actual scope draft. The autonomous route is skeleton → orient → fill section-lazy contracts → soft check → handoff. Tasks belong to scaffold; dialogue ceremony belongs to the optional interactive profile.

BeliefState.Axiom:
The SDD mechanical tools are `gennady` CLI commands. When working IN the gennady repo itself (including any worktree), the runner is `npx tsx /cli/gennady.ts`; in every other project it is `npx gennady`. Thus a Step's canonical `npx gennady ` fixes the command and arguments exactly; substitute only this runner when developing gennady itself, using the current worktree's root. Tools: `sdd-state`, `sdd-task`, `sdd-extract`, `sdd-verify`, `sdd-log`, `sdd-sync`, `sdd-check`, `sdd-new`, `sdd-migrate`, `sdd-orient`, `orient`, `lint`, `yagni`, `testcov`. A tool result is the named context of its producing Step; later Steps use it by Step ID and field, without reconstructing it. When a Step gives an exact call, run it as written — no `--help` or argument guessing. Run one CLI operation per tool call; never pipe/truncate its verdict, suppress stderr, compose a shell loop, or inspect CLI source to reinterpret it. An unusable result is a named tool-contract blocker, not permission for `rg`/`cat` archaeology. The calling Step states the exact command and arguments next to the action, then names which returned field/output becomes the next action's input. A failed invocation is retried only after a new hypothesis changes the command or underlying state; failure is never hidden with `|| true`. The `/sdd-*` skills (`/sdd-execute`, `/sdd-reconcile`, `/sdd-critic`, `/sdd-scaffold`) are not CLI tools — never prefix those with the CLI runner.
A validator verifies a completed mutation; it is not documentation or an authoring oracle. Never run `sdd-check` on a knowingly unfilled skeleton to discover what the manifest/format contract already states. Fill the artifact first, then run the owning Step's exact final check.

Step.Action: Resolve initial/add/refine from disk once. For each new cohesive module, call the ToolCall before reading optional formats. A function/fix scope creates one Function/Service module without invented Port or parallel owner. npx gennady sdd-new module --scope --module Inputs , : scope and cohesive module name resolved in this step. Use moduleManifest.

npx gennady sdd-orient --scope Inputs : scope resolved in STEP_0_CREATE. Use orientation. `sdd-orient` is the only unconditional foreign-context read. Do not load interview, research, or registry protocols unless orientation exposes a real ambiguity.

Keep a closed inventory, one owner for shared files/errors, public surfaces, per-operation DbC, file structure, and negative behavior. Read entity-inventory, entity-surface, and DbC formats only from the comments inside their owning sections, at the moment each section is filled. Remove every instructional comment. The scope owns its requirement IDs. With no narrower obligation write `No module-specific requirements. Implements parent requirements: .` A zero-new-information decision continues without a dialogue stop.

Step.Goal: Make the scope Module Map match actual module files.
Step.Action: Reconcile exact relative links and dependency direction in the scope skeleton's Module Map; never use a separate format file or create two writers for the same map.

npx gennady sdd-check --spec --authoring Inputs : exact path from moduleManifest. Use moduleReceipt. Apply only named hints, then rerun once for the final receipt. For scale=function|fix, check the scope and its one module in this same pass and treat both receipts as one manifest result.

ExecutionPlan.ScalePath: One Function/Service module without invented Port/Adapter; one authoring pass, one combined manifest, no repeated boundary discussion.

Step.Action: Only after the final moduleReceipt has no hints, close authoring atomically. npx gennady sdd-log <module-spec-path> authoring-complete Inputs <module-spec-path>: exact checked path from STEP_4_CHECK. Use moduleAuthoringReceipt.

If an operator explicitly requested live interaction, lazily `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/authoring-interactive.directive.xml")`. Otherwise record deviations and continue to the mechanical close/scaffold route.
